Aerial Wildlife Survey Report  
Wildlife Management Unit 512 Aerial Ungulate Survey (2019-2020) 
 
Background 
Crow Lake Wildlife Management Unit (WMU 512) covers an area of 8,019 km2 and is located north of Lac La 
Biche, Alberta. The unit is bounded to the west by the Athabasca River, and to the south by the 19th baseline.  
The Canadian National railway line that runs through Conklin up to Fort McMurray forms the eastern boundary 
(just west of Highway 881), and the northern boundary is the 21st baseline. 
 
While there are no major population centers within the WMU, Wandering River and Lac La Biche are relatively 
close by. The unit is bisected by Highway 63, which continues north to Fort McMurray. The unit is predominantly 
forested (mostly black spruce interspersed with mixedwood and jack pine stands). Forest harvesting, as well as 
petroleum exploration and extraction, are the most common land uses, and their associated footprints (cut blocks, 
roads, well pads, seismic lines, pipelines, and cutlines) occur throughout the unit, though moreso in the eastern 
portion of the WMU. Portions of both the Cold Lake and East Side Athabasca caribou ranges overlap with the 
WMU. 
 
The objective of the 2020 aerial ungulate survey was to assess the status of the moose population in WMU 512 by 
estimating abundance, density and the age-sex composition. 
 
Survey method 
An aerial survey for ungulates was conducted January 7th to 9th, 2020 using a distance sampling approach 
(Buckland et al., 2001; Thomas et al., 2010). A total of 112 east-west transect lines (survey effort = 994.7 km) were 
flown with two jet ranger helicopters, each outfitted with rear bubble windows to maximize visibility. Moose were 
classified by age class (adult or juvenile) and sex. Other incidental wildlife sightings were also recorded.  
 
Results 
Moose 
A total of 119 moose were observed in 70 groups, which included:  
 
 53 cows 
 40 calves 
 25 bulls (12 antlerless, 13 antlered) 
 one unclassified individual  
 
Estimated density was 0.213 moose/km2 (90% CI 0.155 – 0.293) and estimated abundance was 1,700 individuals 
(90% CI 1,239 – 2,333; Table 1). A total of 118 moose were successfully classified and the bull:cow:calf ratio was 
estimated to be 47:100:75.
